headline: All majors above the 200-day line with RSI deeply overbought, but whale behavior and positioning suggest the rally is losing ballast.
paragraphs: The regime is unified and extended: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, and Doge are all trading above their 200-day moving averages, and all six have MACD above signal line. No golden crosses among them, which means the 50-day has not yet reclaimed the 200-day, so the climb is recent and still within a longer downtrend. Bitcoin sits 36.5 percent below its 12-month high of 124,740, Ethereum 47.9 percent below, and Solana 61 percent below. The reprieve is real, but the hole is deep. Cardano is the outlier, trading below its 200-day with a 76.2 percent drawdown from its 12-month peak, despite a 23 percent bounce over the last week. All this suggests a relief rally inside a larger bear frame, not a regime change.

Momentum is stretched across the board. Bitcoin RSI sits at 82.3, Ethereum at 79.7, Solana at 85.0, XRP at 84.0, BNB at 84.9, and Doge at 78.0. These are the readings you see late in a move, where price has run far enough that even small additional demand shows as extreme overbought. Cardano, with an RSI of 69.1, is the only major with room to run, but it is also the only one below the 200-day. The seven-day and 30-day gains are substantial across the board, with XRP up 50.5 percent in a week and 38.48 percent in a month, Ethereum up 32.36 and 37.87 percent over the same windows. Realized volatility ranges from 32.9 to 80.9 percent, highest in XRP, ADA, and ETH, which is consistent with explosive upside moves. The tape shows a stretched market with little room for acceleration, not a fresh impulsive leg.

Funding rates across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Doge all sit at 0.01 percent per eight hours (annualized to 11 percent), which is moderate to elevated, signaling that long positions are paying to hold the bet. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin has 2.3 billion dollars on OKX, Ethereum 1.48 billion, and smaller caps like Solana, XRP, and Doge between 100 and 275 million. The long-to-short ratio is skewed across smaller caps: Solana 1.93-to-1, XRP 2.09-to-1, Doge 3.47-to-1. Bitcoin and Ethereum are closer to even at 1.01 and 1.08, meaning the leverage is concentrated in the alt chase, not the base. Liquidations over the last 4 to 24 hours show more shorts than longs blown out in Bitcoin and Ethereum (more short liquidations than long), but more longs than shorts in Solana, XRP, and Doge, which means the weak shorts are gone and the long-side risk is now visible. This is a crowded consensus, and the funding is paying long holders to stay in, which typically marks a turn.

Whale behavior is the tell. Over the last 24 hours, 226.5 million dollars moved off exchanges, driven by 146 million in Ethereum outflows from Binance and 80.5 million in Bitcoin net outflows (Binance out 117 million, Kraken out 115 million, offset by 152 million inbound). This looks like accumulation, except for one detail: the weekly trend is collapsing. The week ending August 3 saw 1.085 billion dollars flow off exchanges. The week ending August 10 saw 379 million flow back on. August 17 saw 187 million on. August 24 (the current week) has already moved 864 million back onto exchanges, the largest inflow in the dataset. The daily number is misleading; the weekly sequence tells the real story: whales were accumulating through early August, then have been returning coins to exchanges for three consecutive weeks. That is a distribution posture, not accumulation.

Stablecoin float sits at 308.6 billion dollars and has not moved in 30 days, flat at zero percent change. ETF spot flows remain strong, with Bitcoin taking in 307.5 million on August 21 and 1.92 billion over the last five sessions, all five days in the same direction. Ethereum has taken in 184 million on the latest date and 692.6 million over five sessions. The traditional-finance bid persists, but it is not enough to offset the exchange inflows and the overbought readings. Fear and Greed stands at 73 (Greed) after a 30-day range of 25 to 73, so it is near the top of its window. The crowd is excited, positioning is long and expensive, and the whales have turned net sellers for three weeks.

Watch for a funding rate flip. If the 0.01 percent per eight hours moves negative, longs are no longer paying to stay long, and the convexity disappears. Watch also for the weekly whale flow to reverse back toward off-exchange moves, which would signal a halt to distribution. A break below the 200-day line on any of the majors would confirm the relief rally is complete. Until one of those shifts, the tape reads as a stretched rally inside a bear regime, supported by ETF flows but weakening at the margin as big holders return coins to market.
